title: Cost Signals Observatory: unified telemetry and rollforward playbook for batching, caching, and quant profiles
creator: Priya Sinha
description: Build a cross-team observability and decision playbook (the 'Cost Signals Observatory') that instrumentizes cost/quality telemetry for batching, KV prefetch/caching, and quantization profiles; exposes standardized signals to Console dashboards and the Cost Ops workflow; and provides a gated rollforward playbook to safely expand savings experiments to production. Scope covers SDK + API request metadata, per-route token/cost attribution, per-model quant profile tagging, automatic experiment labels, and a decisionable rollback/rollforward checklist.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console dashboard shows per-route and per-model token cost delta and quality delta for each active experiment window
2) Every batching/cache/quant experiment annotated with consistent tags and experiment IDs in request telemetry
3) Rollforward playbook documented in Confluence with checklist and two-step approval for production rollouts
4) Automated guardrails trigger alerts when quality regression >2% or latency P95 increases >20% during rollout
5) Cross-team signoff (Serving Eng, SRE, Research) completed for at least one pilot rollout
deliverables: Console dashboard widgets: cost delta, quality delta, rollouts panel
Confluence: Cost Signals Observatory playbook and runbook
Automated alerting rule set in PagerDuty/Prometheus
milestones: 2025-01-31: SDK tagging + experiment ID propagation shipped
2025-02-28: Pilot rollforward for internal beta customers
risks: Quality regressions not surfaced quickly enough due to sparse evals
Inconsistent tagging across SDKs leading to noisy signals
Edge cases for hybrid dedicated/private where telemetry constraints exist
notes: Hypothesis: unified telemetry + a clear rollforward playbook will reduce cautious rollout time by >40% while preserving SLAs
We will prioritize routes that account for 60% of hosted token volume for first pilot
Need to align with legal on telemetry retention for Private deployments

open_questions: What thresholds should be used for quality delta across different model families?
How long should the canary observation window be before rollforward by default?
Should we store experiment-level request payloads for debugging in Private deployments? (legal/retention implications)
implementation_notes: Use existing request ID propagation to attach experiment_id and quant_profile meta
Prefer delta-based charts (percent change vs absolute) to normalize across routes
Add a lightweight client-side sampling flag for verbose payloads when investigating regressions
